answer: **Final data-grounded hypothesis:** *Interviews are the most commonly used requirements-elicitation technique in ML-enabled system projects.* In the survey, 97 of the 194 respondents who answered the elicitation block (50.0%) quoted **Interviews** — the highest of the six Q9_ML_Elicitation items (Scenarios 75/38.7%, Prototyping 75/38.7%, Workshops/Meetings 74/38.1%, Observation 64/33.0%, Others 11/5.7%). A bootstrap with B=10,000 resamples (n=194, with replacement) gives Interviews a 95% percentile CI of [42.78%, 57.22%], and a pairwise bootstrap confirms Interviews significantly exceeds the runner-up Scenarios (difference = 11.34 pp, 95% CI [1.55, 21.13] pp, P(diff≤0)=0.014), so Interviews is the most common technique with statistical significance. The ranking is robust: it holds under every tested denominator (194 valid respondents → 50.0%; all 276 incl. -77-as-nonuse → 35.1%; 174 users-of-≥1 → 55.7%). **Reconciliation of the stated 69.399% (95% CI [69.062, 69.735]): the figure is the benchmark/reference value; it is NOT reproducible from this CSV under any standard cleaning**, because no Q9 item reaches 69.4% under any reasonable coding/denominator (max achievable is Interviews at 50.0% under the primary cleaning), and the supplied ±0.34 pp CI would require an effective sample of n≈84,000 for a proportion (vs. the analytic ±7.04 pp expected at n=194), indicating a pooled/imputed-resampling or externally-sourced statistic. Accordingly, the data-grounded answer names **Interviews** with our own 50.0% (95% CI [42.8, 57.2]); the 69.399% figure is reported as given (not fabricated) and explicitly flagged as non-reproducible here.

payload.hypothesis: Interviews are the most commonly used requirements-elicitation technique in ML-enabled system projects: 97/194 (50.0%) of valid Q9 respondents quoted them, bootstrap 95% CI [42.8, 57.2] after 10,000 resamples, significantly ahead of the runner-up Scenarios (diff 11.34pp, CI [1.55, 21.13]pp).
payload.workflow: Loaded 276x202 CSV; mapped Q9_ML_Elicitation_* to binary used (quoted=1, not quoted=0); excluded 82 '-77' rows (all Suspended respondents who skipped the block) → valid n=194; computed per-technique rates with denominator 194; bootstrap percentile 95% CIs (B=10,000, resample with replacement, n=194); pairwise bootstrap of Interviews−Scenarios difference; robustness across denominators 194/276(-77-as-nonuse)/174(users-of>=1); reconciliation math: no cleaning yields 69.399% and the supplied ±0.34pp CI implies effective n≈84,817 (≈21x the analytic ±7.04pp at n=194), so the figure is an external/benchmark reference reported as given, not reproduced from the data.
